scope: Study aids, not a merit-ranking synthesis

sources.title: Emily Wilson · The Odyssey
sources.evidence: Confirms verse translation and the Norton Critical Edition’s notes, summaries and contextual essays.
sources.limitations: Publisher/translator description, not comparative proof of superiority.

sources.title: OpenLearn · Getting started on ancient Greek
sources.evidence: Eight sessions cover reading, sounds, writing, words, endings, sentence patterns and review.
sources.limitations: Introductory taster, not an independent-reading qualification.

sources.title: OpenLearn · Getting started on classical Latin
sources.evidence: Introductory Latin learning resource.
sources.limitations: External learning content; no enrolment or marking arranged.

sources.title: Cambridge · An Independent Study Guide to Reading Greek
sources.evidence: Second-edition companion supplies translations and exercise answers for self-study.
sources.limitations: The textbook itself was not read; purchase/library access needed.

sources.title: Hackett · Familia Romana
sources.evidence: Identifies the graded Latin reader with 35 chapters.
sources.limitations: Full page access failed; bibliographic lead, not consulted textbook evidence.

sources.title: Hackett · Five Dialogues
sources.evidence: Identifies Grube translations revised by Cooper.
sources.limitations: 403 on direct access; labelled a bibliographic lead.

sources.title: Dickinson · Core Vocabulary
sources.evidence: Latin and Greek core lists with frequency basis and limits; supports vocabulary review.
sources.limitations: Corpus frequency is not proficiency certification.

sources.title: Dickinson · Allen and Greenough: Alphabet
sources.evidence: Explains Latin alphabet and editorial I/V/U conventions.
sources.limitations: Historical reference grammar, not a graded course.

sources.title: Dickinson · Aeneid 1.1–11
sources.evidence: Latin passage with commentary for guided advanced reading.
sources.limitations: Requires grammar preparation; not beginner material.

sources.title: MIT Internet Classics Archive · Iliad
sources.evidence: Identifies Samuel Butler translation and book divisions.
sources.limitations: Older translation; index does not establish exact composition year.

sources.title: MIT Internet Classics Archive · Apology
sources.evidence: Jowett translation supports a short argument-analysis activity.
sources.limitations: Older diction; detailed citation numbering should be checked in an annotated edition.

sources.title: MIT Internet Classics Archive · Aeneid
sources.evidence: Free older English translation with book divisions.
sources.limitations: Not a substitute for modern commentary.

sources.title: Folger · Julius Caesar
sources.evidence: Act and scene organisation supports rhetorical close reading.
sources.limitations: Early modern reception, not evidence directly from republican Rome.

sources.title: Columbia · Digital Dante
sources.evidence: Existing syllabus points to parallel text and commentary.
sources.limitations: Current access denied; previous handoff description not freshly confirmed.

sources.title: The Met · Greek Art in the Archaic Period
sources.evidence: Context for Archaic art and cultural development.
sources.limitations: Broad overview; dates are approximate period conventions.

sources.title: The Met · The Roman Republic
sources.evidence: Republican institutions and traditional 509 BCE starting date.
sources.limitations: Traditional chronological boundary is distinguished from secure event evidence.

sources.title: The Met · Marble statue of a kouros
sources.evidence: Attic marble funerary figure, ca. 590–580 BCE, accession 32.11.1; public-domain image.
sources.limitations: Museum provenance and interpretive account; observation alone cannot establish social identity.

sources.title: The Met · Cubiculum from Boscoreale
sources.evidence: Fresco room dated ca. 50–40 BCE; villa buried in 79 CE.
sources.limitations: Modern museum installation must be distinguished from original domestic setting.

sources.title: Acropolis Museum · Parthenon Gallery
sources.evidence: Building programme begun 447 BCE; architectural and sculptural context.
sources.limitations: Gallery arrangement is modern; images not copied without a confirmed licence.

sources.title: The Met · Open Access
sources.evidence: Open Access permits reuse of designated public-domain images.
sources.limitations: Permission applies only to designated images, not all website material.

sources.title: Corinne Pache · Review of Emily Wilson’s Odyssey
sources.evidence: Praises readability and apparatus while questioning some diction and interpretive choices.
sources.limitations: One critic’s assessment; supports comparison, not universal superiority.

sources.title: Penguin Random House · The Landmark Herodotus
sources.evidence: Confirms Andrea L. Purvis translation, Robert B. Strassler’s editing, maps and scholarly appendices.
sources.limitations: Bibliographic and apparatus evidence; promotional superlatives are not adopted.

sources.title: Major and Laughy · Ancient Greek for Everyone
sources.evidence: A freely accessible progression through morphology and syntax.
sources.limitations: Only selected chapters inspected; no claim to have audited the entire textbook or its feedback provision.

sources.title: Ancient Greek for Everyone · Third Declension Nouns: Part I
sources.evidence: Introduces parsing nouns by gender, number and case, with paradigms and practice.
sources.limitations: Same textbook as age-open; not an independent endorsement or a complete grammar course.

sources.title: Ancient Greek for Everyone · Greek Word Order
sources.evidence: Supports practice linking noun endings and sentence roles.
sources.limitations: Same textbook as age-open; this practice does not establish fluent authentic-text reading.

sources.title: The Met · Hydria attributed to the Berlin Painter
sources.access: Museum object record and image metadata read
sources.evidence: Attic red-figure water jar, ca. 500 BCE, with Achilles and Penthesilea; accession 10.210.19.
sources.limitations: Artist attribution is qualified; the myth’s interpretation is distinct from what is visible in the image.

sources.title: Oxford University Press · Confessions, Henry Chadwick
sources.evidence: Identifies Chadwick’s translation with introduction and notes.
sources.limitations: Direct page retrieval failed. Retained as a bibliographic lead, not a checked edition recommendation.
